q2_publishability.reason: The near-complete-split lemma is a substantial proof seed, but the original problem remains open, global novelty has not been exhaustively checked, and the result has not received independent graph-theory review.
q2_publishability.possible_upgrade: A publishable note may become plausible after independent proof audit, literature clearance, and a nontrivial global reduction or additional structural branch.

new_rigorous_results: Near-complete-split branch theorem: if V=C disjoint_union R, R is independent, |C| and |R| are (1/2+o(1))n, delta(G)>=n/2-o(n), and e(G)>floor(n^2/4), then at least n^2/8-o(n^2) edges are pairwise C7-compatible.
The core/hub union construction explicitly covers core-core, same-hub, cross-hub, and core-hub pairs, including equal-row and equal-column degeneracies.
A three-scale cleaning epsilon << rho << tau discards subthreshold low-degree hubs and subthreshold common kernels for only o(n^2) total loss.
The rectangle count reduces to xb+(b-x)(b-x-y)>=b^2/2 when x+y<=b, while x+y>=b is already handled by the hub term.
The induced-matching-only route is invalidated by the Alon--Moitra--Sudakov nearly-complete decomposition construction.
first_strict_breakpoint: There is no proved global reduction taking every strong-induction subproblem of Erdős #809 into the near-complete-split hypotheses. BCM Case 1 can have minimum degree linearly below n/2, and the near-two-clique branch and induction interface remain.
next_decidable_action: Prove a stability/reduction theorem that routes every k=3 induction subproblem either into this split lemma or into a separately controlled near-two-clique family, while preserving the n^2/8-o(n^2) color accounting.
claim_guard: The finite verifier checks displayed C7 templates and arithmetic only. The report proves the asymptotic split lemma, but neither artifact proves the global reduction or closes Erdős #809.
